```

- The "gg" at position 34-35 in the cropped view (starting at col 16) would be at full grid columns 50-51
- The "gg" at position 40-41 in the cropped view would be at full grid columns 56-57

Looking at row 36: `ccNccbbbbccNNNNcccggccccggcccNcc`
Position in cropped: 0=c, 1=c, 2=N, 3=c, 4=c, 5=b, 6=b, 7=b, 8=b, 9=c, 10=c, 11=N, 12=N, 13=N, 14=N, 15=c, 16=c, 17=c, 18=g, 19=g, 20=c, 21=c, 22=c, 23=c, 24=g, 25=g, 26=c, 27=c, 28=c, 29=N, 30=c, 31=c
So the first "gg" is at cropped positions 18-19, which maps to full grid columns 16+18=34 to 16+19=35. That matches the segmentation boundary [[36, 34], [36, 35], [37, 35], [37, 34]].
The second "gg" is at cropped positions 24-25, which maps to full grid columns 16+24=40 to 16+25=41. That matches [[36, 40], [36, 41], [37, 41], [37, 40]].
So the dots ARE at (36, 34) and (36, 40). But clicking there had no impact. Why?

```python
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 36, 'col': 34}, {'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 58, 'col': 52}])
```
The executed actions only show 3 actions total, not 5. This means the first action call was interrupted. But the executed actions show MOUSE(36,34) and MOUSE(36,40) as separate actions. This doesn't match my code...
Oh wait, I see - the previous turn's executed actions were from the previous turn, not the current one. Let me look at what actually happened. The user says "Executed actions: MOUSE(row=36, col=34), MOUSE(row=36, col=40), SPACE." - these are the actions from my LAST code block.
But my code was:
```python
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 36, 'col': 34}, {'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 58, 'col': 52}])
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 36, 'col': 40}, {'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 58, 'col': 38}])
action(['SPACE'])
```
The first call should have executed 2 actions. But the system says only MOUSE(36,34) was executed, then MOUSE(36,40), then SPACE. This means the first action MOUSE(36,34) had no impact and stopped the batch, then MOUSE(58,52) was never executed. Then the second action call started with MOUSE(36,40) which also had no impact...
So the issue is that clicking on the gray dots directly doesn't do anything. The game requires clicking the color FIRST, then the dot. Let me go back to that approach but with intent='solve' to not stop on no-impact.
Actually wait - the FIRST successful placements in level 2 were done with the pattern: click color, then click dot. Those worked. So let me try that again for the remaining dots.
The problem might be that I'm using wrong coordinates. Let me double-check:
- Yellow block: [57,51]-[60,54], center would be (58, 52) or (59, 52)
- Pink block: [57,37]-[60,40], center would be (58, 38) or (59, 38)
For the successful placements earlier:
- Blue at [57,44]-[60,47], clicked (58, 45) - worked
- Green at [57,23]-[60,26], clicked (58, 24) - worked
So the pattern is: row = top+1, col = left+1. For yellow: row=58, col=52. For pink: row=58, col=38.
Let me try again with intent='solve' to bypass the no-impact check.
Actually wait, I just realized - maybe the issue is that the order of colors to fill is wrong. The top pattern is O, p, R, b, N, Y, M. But I filled:
- Red container: O, p, R (skipping the charcoal slot)
- Green container: b, N
So the remaining should be Y, M for the last two green dots. But maybe the charcoal slot in the red container is actually a slot that needs to be filled too? Let me reconsider.
Looking at the top pattern: O, p, R, b, N, Y, M (7 colors)
The red container has 4 slots: dot1, dot2, charcoal_slot, dot3
The green container has 4 slots: dot1, dot2, dot3, dot4
If the charcoal slot is already "filled" (or is a special slot), then:
- Red: 3 fillable slots
- Green: 4 fillable slots
- Total: 7 slots for 7 colors
I filled red with O, p, R and green with b, N. Remaining: Y, M for green dots 3 and 4.
But clicking on the dots directly didn't work. The game requires color-then-dot. Let me try that with intent='solve'.
